content.comment_body: Is it possible to set the real-time clock of the [product_name] using NTP protocol over Ethernet? If this is not supported, how is long-term clock accuracy maintained?

Hello, Based on my experience, this is not supported. You can synchronize the clock using [product_name] Soft Comfort and LAN. All modules in the same subnet will receive the same settings, or you can use KNX/EIB, but you need to enable time and date synchronization in the [product_name] basis module settings. Hope this helps.

So, a device capable of NTP (like a Linux box) could send KNX packets to the [product_name] for time synchronization? It seems complex, but could be more reliable than manual adjustment. Does anyone know of a PLC that supports NTP? Using Ethernet for this would be one of my first priorities.

Hello, There is another alternative. You can connect the [product_name] [article_no] to a WLAN router and use the [company_name] app to synchronize date and time with your mobile device. If your mobile device is accurately set, you can use it for synchronization. More details are available on the [company_name] product website. Hope this is helpful.

Thank you for the suggestion. It's interesting, but ideally, I want the PLCs to run for years without intervention and still maintain the correct time. Regularly logging in for time updates isn't a practical long-term solution.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the long-term timekeeping accuracy of the [product_name], noting that it cannot automatically synchronize its real-time clock using NTP protocol over Ethernet. Current methods require manual input or external systems like KNX or mobile apps to synchronize time, which many find inconvenient for unattended systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the PLC to automatically maintain accurate time, preferably with NTP synchronization via Ethernet, and without the need for ongoing manual adjustments.
